title: Transactional change replay + graceful rewind for config applies
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build an automated, transactional 'apply+replay' mechanism for config changes that can safely detect regressions (cost, latency, errors) and perform a graceful rewind (partial or full) with state reconciliation. This covers batching/cache-related config (batch window, max-batch-size, prefix cache TTLs), routing policies, autoscaling thresholds, and model-variant fallbacks.

Why: Recent incidents where rapid config churn or aggressive batching tuned in prod caused token-cost spikes or latency SLO violations. We need an automated safety layer that treats config changes like transactions with checkpoints and a deterministic rewind path, minimizing blast radius while preserving customer-specific tuning.

Scope:
- A transaction semantics for grouped config changes (apply as unit with pre-apply simulation and post-apply monitoring window).
- Multiple trigger signals (cost delta, latency, error rate, request-rate mismatch) that can initiate automated rewind.
- Guardrails including dry-run simulation, staged replay (shadow / canary / full), and economic hysteresis to avoid oscillation.
- State reconciliation engine that computes three-way diffs (desired, last-applied, live) and applies minimal reverse ops.
- Observable audit trail and incident metadata for each auto-rewind for post-mortem and product team feedback.

Non-goals: Autoscaling algorithm redesign; integrating with external customer CI for policy-as-code (this will come later). This ticket focuses on the orchestration and safe revert logic, not on comprehensive UI for policy editing.
acceptance_criteria: Config applies can be created as a single transactional bundle (API + Console).
Pre-apply simulation runs and produces a delta estimate (expected token-cost change and latency risk) shown in the API response and console before commit.
Post-apply monitoring window (configurable per-bundle) evaluates signals and can trigger automated rewind within the window.
Automated rewind performs minimal state changes to restore last-known-good behavior, with zero orphaned routing entries and consistent KV cache boundaries.
Three-way reconciliation report available after rewind showing which keys changed, which were reverted, and why (cost/latency/error).
End-to-end E2E test harness demonstrates a staged apply -> canary -> triggered-rewind scenario in CI with <5% flaky runs.
implementation_notes: Transaction model: create ConfigBundle object with mutation list + metadata (owner, reason, dry_run_flag, rollback_window_seconds). Persist bundle as immutable snapshot in config-store.
Simulation: run synthetic lightweight traffic using request-profiles sampled from route-heatmap. Produce cost delta estimate via simulator (uses batching simulator module).
Triggers: cost_delta_pct, p95_latency_delta_ms, error_rate_delta_pct, request_pattern_shift_score. Each trigger configurable per-org with thresholds and weighting.

Rewind strategy: compute three-way diff between desired (bundle), last_applied(snapshot), live(state). Generate reverse-ops in idempotent order; use checkpointed steps with commit tokens to allow retry and resume.
Hysteresis: require at least 2 consecutive monitoring windows breaching threshold OR a high-confidence single breach (cost > 150% baseline) before auto-rewind to avoid oscillation.
KV cache boundary handling: when rolling back cache TTLs or prefix cache enabling, issue a cache-invalidation job for affected shards to prevent cache poisoning/serving inconsistency.
Observability: emit per-bundle events to console (events: SIMULATION_DONE, APPLIED, CANARY_METRIC, REWIND_INIT, REWIND_STEP, REWIND_COMPLETE) with links to dashboards/PRs.
Security: ensure the auto-rewind runbook runs under least privilege and records KMS/credential actions in audit log.
tasks: Design data model for ConfigBundle + snapshotting (RFC in Confluence).
Implement simulation harness that consumes route heatmaps and returns token-cost/latency delta estimates (backend).
Implement trigger evaluation service and config for per-org thresholds (backend).
Build reconciliation engine to compute three-way diffs and generate reverse ops (backend & runbook).
Add cache-invalidation primitives to orchestration layer and test on staging clusters.
Integrate event emission with Console UI and add a minimal bundle timeline view (frontend).
Create CI E2E test scenarios that simulate spike and ensure automated rewind path works.
Create runbook and post-mortem template for auto-rewind incidents, include cost and latency artifacts.
risks: False positives in triggers causing unnecessary rewinds; mitigated via hysteresis and multi-signal weighting.
Incomplete reverse ops leaving stale routing entries causing traffic loss; mitigated with idempotent ordering and post-rewind validation checks.
Simulator inaccuracies underrepresenting tail latency; will progressively tune using canary telemetry and A/B comparisons.
Customer-specific overrides (manual pinning of model versions) may conflict with automated rewind; ensure we honor explicit customer locks in bundle evaluation.
metrics: % of auto-rewinds that prevented a >25% cost spike (goal: >=90%).
Mean time to detect and begin rewind (target < 3 minutes).
Rate of false-positive rewinds per 1k applies (target < 1).
Post-rewind health check pass rate (target 100% for critical routes).
Simulated delta vs observed delta divergence (target < 15%).
